pr.title: Only track mentioned places for jump threading
pr.description:
This PR aims to reduce the state space size in jump threading and dataflow const-prop opts.

The current implementation walks the types of all locals, and creates a place for each possible projection. This can easily lead to a large number of places and tracked values, most being useless to the actual pass.

With this PR, we instead collect places that appear syntactically in the MIR (first commit). However, this is not sufficient (second commit), and we miss places that we could track in aggregate assignments. The third commit tracks such assignments to mirror place projections, see the inline comment.

This is complementary to https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/127036

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The historical change is an optimization-coverage fix in `value_analysis::Map`, not a semantics-changing source rewrite. The "incorrect" intermediate transformation (syntactic-only place collection without the aggregate-assignment mirroring fixpoint) merely fails to register places such as `_1.1` that are reachable only through a whole-aggregate copy. In `State::get`/`try_get`, an unregistered place yields top/unknown, so DataflowConstProp conservatively leaves the copy and condition unfolded and JumpThreading conservatively leaves the `switchInt` in place. The generated program still computes the same result; the PR itself and the frozen pitfalls state that missing mirrored places are expected to reduce optimization coverage rather than directly produce a wrong constant. The decoded diff confirms this: before/after the replacement pass the control flow and returned values remain consistent, with the only difference being whether the condition is folded or the branch threaded. Therefore there is no concrete defined input on which the original all-projection registration and the syntactic-only transformation produce different original/transformed return values. Constructing such a pair would require inventing an unrelated semantic change, which the task forbids. No source-grounded counterexample can be validated.

analysis.originalLogic: The old `value_analysis::Map` built places by walking the types of all locals: it started with a worklist of bare locals, registered enum `Discriminant` places, slice `DerefLen` places, and recursively enqueued every field via `iter_fields`, allocating a scalar value slot whenever the layout had scalar ABI. The PR describes this as: “The current implementation walks the types of all locals, and creates a place for each possible projection. This can easily lead to a large number of places and tracked values, most being useless to the actual pass.”
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically insufficient replacement is to register only places that occur syntactically in the MIR, without the subsequent assignment-mirroring fixpoint. Under that transformation, for `_1 = const Foo; _2 = _1; _3 = (_2.1: u32);`, only `_2.1` is seen syntactically; `_1.1` is not registered even though `_2` is a whole-aggregate copy of `_1`. Consequently DataflowConstProp cannot carry the known scalar through the copy, so the `_2` assignment and the condition on `_3` are not folded, and JumpThreading leaves the `switchInt` in place. The corrected implementation additionally records assignment pairs for `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Move|Copy)`, `Rvalue::CopyForDeref`, and non-union `Rvalue::Aggregate`, then mirrors child projections in both directions to a fixpoint before allocating scalar value slots. This is explicitly acknowledged in the PR: “With this PR, we instead collect places that appear syntactically in the MIR (first commit). However, this is not sufficient (second commit), and we miss places that we could track in aggregate assignments.”
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR bodies containing local aggregates—tuples, structs, arrays, enums, closures, coroutines, etc.—where an aggregate is assigned as a whole (constant aggregate, `Aggregate` rvalue, or copy/move between locals) and a scalar field, enum discriminant, or slice length is then read through a copy. The distinguishing input is a scalar reachable only through an aggregate-copy alias, e.g. `let a = Foo; let b = a; let c = b.1; if c == 2 { b.0 } else { 13 }`, or the MIR pattern `_1 = (const 5u32, const 13i64); _2 = _1; _3 = (_2.0 as u32);` where `_1.0` never appears syntactically. Unions are outside the aggregate-mirroring domain.
analysis.summary: Restrict `value_analysis::Map` place registration from all type-derived projections to syntactic MIR places plus assignment-derived mirror places, while preserving propagation through whole-aggregate copies for DataflowConstProp and JumpThreading. The key reusable lesson is that syntactic-only tracking is insufficient: aggregate-copy assignments require a bidirectional child-mirroring fixpoint.
analysis.trigger: A condition or use reads a scalar field/discriminant/slice length through a whole-aggregate copy rather than directly from the local whose aggregate value is known. With syntactic-only place registration, the source child place is absent from the map; with the mirroring fixpoint, it is registered and DataflowConstProp can fold values and JumpThreading can simplify the branch.
preconditions: The base local must be tracked in `Map::locals`; unsupported locals or projections cause `register_place` to return `None`.
A syntactic-use collector must still register assignment LHS/RHS places separately, because `visit_place` only acts when `ctxt.is_use()`.
Recognized aggregate-preserving assignments are `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Move|Copy)`, `Rvalue::CopyForDeref`, and `Rvalue::Aggregate`; unions are deliberately excluded.
For enum aggregates, descend through `TrackElem::Variant(variant)` before registering field children.
Mirror children from LHS to RHS and from RHS to LHS, repeating until the number of places stabilizes, so multi-step copy chains are covered.
Allocate scalar `ValueIndex` slots only after the place set is stable; otherwise newly mirrored children would lack value slots.
When a registered place is an enum or a slice reference/raw pointer, eagerly register its typed `Discriminant` or `DerefLen` child.
pitfalls: Do not replace all-projections registration with purely syntactic collection; the PR's own first commit was insufficient because fields reachable only through aggregate copies were missed.
Do not mirror only one direction or only one iteration: a fixpoint is required, and each newly created child pair must itself be inserted into the assignment set.
Do not propagate aggregate fields through unions; the patch explicitly says `// Do not propagate unions.`
For enums built with `AggregateKind::Adt(_, variant, _, _, None)`, first register the variant projection; otherwise field indices are attached at the wrong level.
Do not allocate scalar values during place discovery: value slots must be created after all mirrored places exist.
Missing mirrored places are expected to reduce optimization coverage rather than directly produce a wrong constant; untracked places are treated as unknown/top by the value analysis.
The map now carries the lifetime/type parameter of the body (`Map<'tcx>`/`PlaceInfo<'tcx>`), so child registration must preserve the source place's type when mirroring to the destination.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused `tests/mir-opt` tests for both passes. For DataflowConstProp, use `//@ test-mir-pass: DataflowConstProp` and `// EMIT_MIR aggregate_copy.foo.DataflowConstProp.diff` with a constant tuple, a whole-value copy, and a later field read: `const Foo: (u32, u32) = (5, 3); let a = Foo; let b = a; let c = b.1; if c >= 2 { b.0 } else { 13 }`. Check that the copy becomes `const (5_u32, 3_u32)`, the field read becomes `const 3_u32`, and the condition becomes `const true`. Also cover the direct aggregate-assignment shape `_1 = (const 5u32, const 13i64); _2 = _1; _3 = (_2.0 as u32);` so `_1.0` is required despite not being syntactic. For JumpThreading, add the same aggregate-copy pattern to `tests/mir-opt/jump_threading.rs`, emit both panic-abort and panic-unwind diffs, and assert `CHECK-NOT: switchInt(` so the copied-field condition is threaded; the added test is described as “Verify that jump threading succeeds seeing through copies of aggregates.” Include negative coverage for unions and for unsupported projections if extending the collector.
